# Data Description

We use the public oregon population and oregon sample data from the FIA. These have, respectively, auxiliary variables measured at the pixel-level throughout Oregon, and tagged observations of biomass with auxiliary data measured sparsely throughout Oregon. The population data are a small subset of 200,000 of the approximate 31,000,000 pixels within Oregon.

To assist with stability and reduce variability of priors, we will scale the `elev` and the `ppt` variables to have a smaller variance.

```{r}
data("oregon_population", "oregon_sample")
# sapply(oregon_sample, sd) # find variables with large variances

oregon_population$elev <- oregon_population$elev / sd(oregon_sample$elev)
oregon_sample$elev <- oregon_sample$elev / sd(oregon_sample$elev)

oregon_population$ppt <- oregon_population$ppt / sd(oregon_sample$ppt)
oregon_sample$ppt <- oregon_sample$ppt / sd(oregon_sample$ppt)
```

# Model Specification

We propose three models: A normal BHF, a FH, and a zero-inflated BHF. The two BHFs will have a fourth-root transform to help model fitness

```{r}
model_formula <- biomass ~ evc + ppt
trans <- transform(
  function(y) {y^(1/4)},
  function(y) {y^4}
)
BHF_spec <- specify(
  model_formula, domain_name = "evt",
  model = "BHF", transform = trans
)
FH_spec <- specify(model_formula, domain_name = "evt", model = "FH")
ZI_spec <- specify(model_formula,
  domain_name = "evt", model = "BHF",
  transform = trans, model_stage = "zi"
)
```

To facilitate fitting the FH, we will aggregate the data, with the population size as approximately 31 million:

```{r}
agg_data <- aggregate(
  oregon_sample, "biomass", "evt", oregon_population,
  population_size = 31000000
)
```


```{r}
BHF_fit <- fit(BHF_spec, oregon_sample, verbose = FALSE)
FH_fit <- fit(FH_spec, agg_data, verbose = FALSE)
ZI_fit <- fit(ZI_spec, oregon_sample, verbose = FALSE)
```

```{r}
check(BHF_fit)
check(FH_fit)
check(ZI_fit)
```

The first model has poor fitness but we proceed anyway.

```{r}
stats <- c(
  mean = mean,
  se = sd,
  lower_95_ci = lower_ci_quantile(0.95),
  upper_95_ci = upper_ci_quantile(0.95)
)
BHF_preds <- estimate(
  BHF_fit,
  newdata = oregon_population,
  domain = "county",
  ndraws = 500,
  stat = stats
)
FH_preds <- estimate(
  FH_fit,
  domain = "county",
  ndraws = 500,
  stat = stats
)
ZI_preds <- estimate(
  ZI_fit,
  newdata = oregon_population,
  domain = "county",
  ndraws = 500,
  stat = stats
)
```

The estimates can be joined and then viewed for any county:
```{r}
comparisons <- left_join(
  left_join(
    BHF_preds$preds, FH_preds$preds,
    suffix = c("_BHF", "_FH"),
    by = "county"
  ),
  ZI_preds$preds,
  suffix = c("", "_ZI"),
  by = "county"
)

head(comparisons)
```

We observed some issues with model fitting here, as evidenced by some of the warnings. These may be improved via prior specification, other variable transforms, other model specifications, and other covariates.
